question.worked_solution:
Let $u={log}_{5}⁡(5x).$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{5x\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\cdot 5=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡5\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $1$ | $5$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $2$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{5}\frac{7{log}_{5}⁡(5x)}{x}\,\text{d}x & =7{\int }_{1}^{5}{log}_{5}⁡(5x)\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =7{\int }_{1}^{2}u\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡5\,\text{d}u \\  & =7\operatorname{ln}⁡5{\int }_{1}^{2}u\,\text{d}u \\  & =7\operatorname{ln}⁡5\cdot \frac{{u}^{2}}{2}{|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =7\operatorname{ln}⁡5\cdot (\frac{4}{2}-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{21\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
